post.caption: A hand crank cuts guilloché patterns. Guilloché is a pattern cut into metal by a rose engine. The machine rocks the metal against a patterned disc called a rosette. A straight line machine cuts straight lines, like Clous de Paris. Both are cranked by hand while the other hand guides the cutter. The grooves are only 30 to 40 microns deep. Translucent enamel is fused over the cuts, so the pattern shows through. Fabergé used the same trick from the 1880s. Breguet made engine turned watch dials famous from 1786. Workshops still cut dials on machines more than a century old.
